data.name: HelpIntro
data.value: This page explains the workflow and the settings that visibly change the result. Everything refers to the spectrum that is currently selected.

data.name: HelpQStart
data.value: How do I analyze a spectrum?

data.name: HelpAStart
data.value: 1. Check the model: the "Model" card shows whether an ONNX model is loaded. If not, load one in Settings (button in the top right). 2. Open an MGF: "Open MGF" reads every spectrum of the file. Title, precursor mass and, when present, SMILES are taken over. 3. Select a spectrum: click or tap the entry in the list. 4. Enter a candidate: type a SMILES into the "Candidate" card. Formula and precursor m/z are derived from it and can be overridden; the adduct is selectable. 5. Analyze: "Analyze" starts the prediction. The peak table, structure view and ranking fill in afterwards. 6. Repeat: change the SMILES and analyze again to test another candidate against the same measurement. The score is only meaningful in comparison.

data.name: HelpQScore
data.value: What does the FLARE score tell me?

data.name: HelpAScore
data.value: The score is the similarity between the measured spectrum and the predicted fragment peaks of the entered structure. It ranges from 0 to 1; higher is better. It is meant as a relative comparison: when you test several candidates, the order shows which structure explains the measurement best. A single score without competitors is no proof of identity, because constitutional isomers with the same mass often produce very similar values. The ranking additionally shows the rank, the distance to the best candidate (delta) and a star for the reference structure from the file.

data.name: HelpQPeaks
data.value: What do the peak table columns mean?

data.name: HelpAPeaks
data.value: - m/z: calculated fragment mass with four decimals. - Formula: molecular formula of the fragment. An empty cell means the peak could not be explained. - Int. %: relative intensity against the base peak (100 %). A dash means the peak is not present in the measured spectrum. - Weight: the normalized match value between 0 and 1 for the current selection. It drives the colour in the table, the spectrum and the structure. The precursor peak is marked separately and excluded from the ranking, because it carries no fragment information. Clicking a row selects that peak and highlights the matching atoms in the structure.

data.name: HelpQNormalization
data.value: What do the normalization modes and the softmax temperature do?

data.name: HelpANormalization
data.value: Normalization defines how the atom similarity values are mapped onto the colour range. Three modes are available: - Global min-max: minimum and maximum over the whole similarity matrix. This matches the original FLARE. Drawback: one single very good atom-peak match pushes all other colours down. - Per-peak min-max: every peak row is scaled on its own. The best atom of each peak is therefore always fully saturated, so you can see which atom fits best for that peak even when the peak itself is only weakly explained. - Softmax: atoms compete per peak through a softmax function, then the result is divided by the global maximum. This gives the sharpest contrast: a clearly leading atom gets nearly the full colour, close contenders fade quickly. The softmax temperature controls how sharp that competition is. Small values (around 0.01) emphasize only the clear winner, larger values (up to 0.5) spread the colour across similarly good atoms. The slider is only shown while softmax is selected. The choice is saved and restored on the next start.

data.name: HelpAThreshold
data.value: The threshold hides weak matches: atoms and peaks with a weight below the value are drawn in neutral grey instead of a colour. Low (0): the full colour ramp is visible, including noise. High (around 0.5): only clear matches keep their colour, the picture becomes calmer and easier to read. The threshold does not change the calculated weights. It only decides whether colour is applied, and it can be reverted at any time.

data.name: HelpAColormap
data.value: The colormap defines the colour ramp for the weights: Viridis, Plasma, Inferno, Magma and Turbo. The bar below shows the ramp from "low" (0) to "high" (1). Viridis and Inferno remain distinguishable with colour vision deficiency, Turbo has the strongest contrast, Plasma and Magma sit in between. The choice is purely visual: it changes no number, only the colour.

data.name: HelpQStructure
data.value: How do I read the structure view?

data.name: HelpAStructure
data.value: The drawing shows the candidate with atoms coloured by their weight. - Click or tap an atom: that atom becomes selected and the peak table shows the weight of this atom per peak. - Without a selection the maximum across all atoms applies, i.e. the best match of the peak. - Hover over the drawing (desktop): peaks that match the atom under the pointer are highlighted. - Click beside the molecule: clear the selection. Below the drawing, buttons list all heavy atoms with their label (for example C3) and weight; they behave like the atoms in the drawing. Rendering is done by MolDraw on top of SkiaSharp.

data.name: HelpQPlot
data.value: How do I operate the spectrum plot?

data.name: HelpAPlot
data.value: - Click or tap a peak: select it. - Drag: pan horizontally. - Mouse wheel (desktop): zoom around the pointer position. - Double click or double tap: reset the zoom. - Hover over the plot: peaks under the pointer are emphasized. The buttons "Reset zoom", "Zoom to peak" and "Clear selection" below the plot do the same. On a phone, tapping and dragging work; use the buttons to zoom.

data.name: HelpQCandidates
data.value: How do I test several candidates at once?

data.name: HelpACandidates
data.value: The "Candidates" card lets several structures compete. - Paste SMILES, one line per candidate. Empty lines and comments are ignored. - "From MGF" takes the SMILES annotations of the opened file as the candidate list. - "Only matching mass" removes candidates whose precursor mass does not fit the measurement. This saves a lot of compute time on long lists. - "Ranking" runs the analysis for every candidate. The result shows rank, score, distance to the best candidate (delta) and a star for the reference structure. Select a row to load that candidate into the structure and peak table. Depending on the number of candidates the ranking takes a few seconds; the status line reports progress.

data.name: HelpQManual
data.value: I have no MGF, only a peak list.

data.name: HelpAManual
data.value: Use the "Manual spectrum" card for that. - Enter m/z values and intensities separately; separators may be semicolons, commas or line breaks. - Decimal separator: both point and comma are accepted. - Both lists must have the same length, otherwise an error message appears. The manual spectrum is added to the spectrum list and can be analyzed like an MGF spectrum. A candidate in the "Candidate" card is required, because the prediction needs a structure.

data.name: HelpAModel
data.value: FLARE computes with an ONNX model, flare.onnx by default. In Settings you can type a path, browse for a file or restore the default path. The status line names the loaded state. Without a loaded model you can still draw structures, but no predictions are computed. The path is saved and loaded automatically on the next start.

data.name: HelpQPlatform
data.value: Why is the prediction missing on some devices?

data.name: HelpAPlatform
data.value: The app runs on Windows (x64 and ARM64) and on Android. Prediction from MGF and peak data needs the chemistry engine (RDKit with native libraries). It is currently only included in the Windows x64 build, which offers the full feature set. On Windows ARM64 and on Android, spectrum management, visualization, ranking logic and structure drawing remain available; for the model prediction the app reports that RDKit is missing. Use the Windows x64 build if you need that part.

data.name: HelpQLanguage
data.value: How do I switch the language?

data.name: HelpALanguage
data.value: In Settings with the "Deutsch" and "English" buttons. The switch applies immediately to all texts, including this help, and is saved. Measurements and inputs keep point and semicolon regardless of the language so they stay compatible with MGF files. A comma is also accepted while typing.
